snomed_ct: Broad clinical terminology; MRCM-governed concept model spanning findings, disorders, procedures, body structures, organisms, substances and qualifiers.
hpo: Narrow but deep phenotype ontology; Phenotypic abnormality branch with modifiers and disease/gene annotations.
interoperability_implication: SNOMED CT is broader; HPO is deeper for phenotype analysis. Bridge by workflow-specific mappings, not interchange.

snomed_ct: Subtype polyhierarchy; distinction between primitive and sufficiently defined concepts via necessary-and-sufficient conditions.
hpo: DAG (ontology graph); curated is_a structure with entity-quality style logical definitions where release coverage allows.
interoperability_implication: Definition sufficiency and graph shape differ; subsumption must be interpreted per resource.

snomed_ct: Attributes with MRCM domains, ranges, cardinalities, and relationship groups enforced at authoring time.
hpo: OBO relations and entity-quality logical definitions reusing external ontologies (e.g., Uberon, PATO).
interoperability_implication: Constraints are implemented through different artifacts and must be translated, not copied.

snomed_ct: Severity, clinical course and similar modifiers via attributes and, in many areas, pre-coordinated concepts.
hpo: Onset, severity, frequency and temporality separated into dedicated branches / annotation structures (post-coordination).
interoperability_implication: Pre- vs post-coordination is the main source of modifier information loss during transformation.

snomed_ct: Mappings, cross-references and shared use in clinical-genomic workflows; directional, versioned claims.
hpo: Curated xrefs (incl. SNOMEDCT_US), UMLS co-location, Monarch crosswalks and semantic-similarity tooling.
interoperability_implication: Cross-references are curated semantic claims with provenance, not symmetric synonyms.

snomed_ct: OWL 2 EL classification and subsumption for terminology maintenance and release QA.
hpo: Classification, consistency checking and, distinctively, semantic similarity over phenotype profiles.
interoperability_implication: Reasoning serves terminology maintenance in one resource and phenotype comparison in the other.
